idea: Two lines have no solution when they are parallel (same slope, different intercept) and infinitely many when they are the same line. In coefficient form, the equations' x-, y- and constant terms must be in the same ratio for infinitely many solutions; only the x and y ratios match for none.
trap: Solving k2= something and keeping both signs. Check each value against the constants' ratio; one sign often gives parallel lines instead.
desmos: A slider for k lets you watch the lines turn parallel, but reading an exact value off a slider is slow and risky. Matching ratios takes one line of algebra.

items.stem:
In the system below, a is a constant.
ax+7y=15 21x+21y=12 For what value of a does the system have no solution?
items.explain: No solution means the lines are parallel: the x- and y-coefficients are in the same ratio, but the constants are not. The y-coefficients are in the ratio 7:21=1:3, so a=321​=7. The constants are 15 and 12, not in the ratio 1:3, so the lines don't coincide.

items.stem:
In the system below, k is a constant.
kx+4y=24 9x+ky=36 For what value of k does the system have infinitely many solutions?
items.explain: Infinitely many solutions needs all three ratios equal: 9k​=k4​=3624​. From the first two, k2=36, so k=±6. The constants' ratio is 3624​=32​, which matches 9k​ only when k=6. With k=−6, the lines are parallel and there is no solution.

items.stem:
In the system below, a and b are constants and a>0.
ax+2y=25 15x+(a+1)y=b If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of a+b?
items.explain: The equations must be multiples of each other: 15a​=a+12​=b25​. From the first two, a(a+1)=30, so a=5 (the other root is negative). Then b25​=155​, so b=75, and a+b=80.
